segments.content:
Chapter 122: Defeat You With Your Own Magic

Qianjiang University's family housing district was located on the north side, near the bank of the Yin River.

Xu Youyu led them in through the district entrance, and they soon arrived downstairs. They then took the elevator to the fifth floor.

Taking out her key to open the door, Xu Youyu retrieved some shoe covers from a cabinet and called toward the kitchen, "Mom! I'm home!"

Hearing the commotion at the door, Cui Suling quickly came out of the kitchen, greeting them with a beaming smile, "Hello, hello, come in and have a seat anywhere. Dinner will be a little while. Youyu, keep our guests company first."

"I know."

At this point, Li Luo, having put on his shoe covers, picked up the fruit he had brought and followed Cui Suling to the kitchen. "Auntie, where would be a good place for this fruit?"

"Oh my, why did you bring something?" Cui Suling hurriedly refused. "You're all too kind."

"It's what we should do," Li Luo said with a cheerful smile. "Senior Sister said these are all things you and Uncle enjoy. I'll just leave them here for you to try later."

"Youyu, honestly. Not only did you not refuse, you even helped him pick them out." Cui Suling shot her daughter a look and took the fruit from Li Luo, planning to put it in the refrigerator first.

Xu Youyu stood frozen in place, wondering how she had become the one who picked them out.

Li Luo had clearly been the one who made the selections so decisively!

Who knew what kind of luck he had to pick out everything the two of you liked.

"Alright, go sit in the living room. It's smoky in the kitchen," Cui Suling said, calling out after thanking Li Luo. "Youyu, take them on a little tour. You can check out the balcony."

"Okay."

Xu Youyu answered and then led them toward the balcony.

The apartment in the Xu family's building wasn't particularly large, probably around seventy or eighty square meters.

Besides a small living room and kitchen, there was a master bedroom, a secondary bedroom, and a small study.

It wasn't big, but it was very cozy. The entire place was cleaned and tidied in an orderly fashion, and traces of life could be seen everywhere.

And the balcony in Xu Youyu's home was a place she took every guest to visit.

"Uncle, Auntie, look."

Xu Youyu pushed open the window and pointed outside.

Their apartment window faced west. To the right, one could see the Yin River and the cross-river bridge not far away, a uniquely beautiful view.

And to the right, one could also overlook a small half of Qianjiang University.

"That's the north gate of Qianjiang University. Usually, only a small side gate is open, mostly for people from the family housing district to come and go."

"That area inside is the north-side sports field. My dad's office in the School of Liberal Arts is in that building right next to it, which is quite close to home."

"And that tallest building is Qianjiang University's landmark library. Next to it is a man-made lake, filled with water diverted from a tributary of the Yin River. It's called Qiuzhen Lake."

"Of all the things to teach, teach people to seek truth; of all the things to learn, learn to be a true person."

"That's the meaning behind Qiuzhen Lake."

"Well said." Lin Xiuhong gazed at Qianjiang University in the distance, her heart filled with longing. She couldn't help but praise, "Youyu, you know so much."

"You're too kind, Auntie. I grew up here. When I was little, my dad would tell me these things all day long, I'm sick of hearing them," Xu Youyu said with a laugh. "I used to play all over inside, so I'm pretty familiar with it."

"That's wonderful," Lin Xiuhong remarked with a sigh. She then looked at Li Luo and urged, "If you maintain your current grades, you should be able to get into Qianjiang University. You have to make us proud."

"Don't worry, Auntie," Xu Youyu said with a smile. "As long as Li Luo maintains his current scores, Qianjiang University will be a breeze."

If someone in the top 30 of the entire school still couldn't get into Qianjiang University, then it wouldn't be Li Luo's problem, but No. 1 Affiliated High School's problem.

The group gazed at Qianjiang University from the balcony for a while. After sitting back down on the living room sofa, Ying Chanxi sat next to Yan Zhusheng, placing herself right between her and Li Luo.

She then began chatting with Yan Zhusheng with a normal expression.

"Have you considered what university you want to attend in the future, Zhusheng?" Ying Chanxi asked curiously.

"The Central Conservatory of Music, or the Changning Conservatory of Music," Yan Zhusheng said after a moment's thought. "The Qianjiang Conservatory of Music is also very good, and it's affiliated with Qianjiang University."

"That's right," Xu Youyu added from the side. "The conservatory is on the westernmost side. We can't see it from our place, or I would have pointed it out to you just now."

"So you're planning to apply as an arts student?" Li Guohong asked, his gaze falling on Yuan Wanqing, and he couldn't help but chuckle. "That makes sense. After all, your mother... hmm... your mother raised you well. You sang very well today."

"Wouldn't it be a waste if she didn't apply as an arts student?" Li Luo said, sitting beside them. "Her regular academic scores definitely aren't enough for Qianjiang University right now, but if her scores in the unified and school-specific exams are up to standard, then her current academic scores are more than enough, to say the least."

Hearing Li Luo say this, Ying Chanxi bit her lip slightly and subconsciously glanced at him.

Yan Zhusheng, however, was completely oblivious and just earnestly held Ying Chanxi's hand. "I'll work hard, so we can still go to the same university in the future."

"Mm... yeah." Ying Chanxi pursed her lips. Suddenly feeling Yan Zhusheng's sincerity, she felt a bit dazed.

She always felt that Yan Zhusheng was a bit ditsy sometimes; she really didn't know what was on her mind.

Ying Chanxi thought of the Pikachu on her bedside table, and her body instantly softened. After the emotions in her eyes gradually subsided, she let out a soft sigh.

Just then, there was a sound at the door.

Xu Rongsheng pushed open the door and saw the living room full of guests. He immediately said with a smile, "I'm so sorry, I just finished up with things at the university and came back late."

"It's no problem, no problem at all." Li Guohong was the first to stand up, taking two steps forward to shake his hand. "Hello, I'm Li Luo's father, and this is his mother."

"And this is Ying Chanxi. Next to her are Yan Zhusheng and Yan Zhusheng's mother."

"We just arrived not long ago ourselves. We were looking at the view from the balcony. The feng shui of your home is incredible. You can see Qianjiang University at a glance."

After the two sides exchanged pleasantries, Xu Rongsheng changed into slippers, put his briefcase in the study, and took off his jacket before returning to the living room to chat with the other parents.

So Xu Youyu simply called Li Luo and the other two over to hang out in the study, where they could at least play on the computer for a while.

After another half hour, Cui Suling finished cooking and came to call them for dinner.

A total of nine people sat in a circle around the table. Xu Rongsheng poured a small cup of baijiu for Li Guohong and then invited everyone to start eating.

Perhaps it was because of the invitation letter from that afternoon, or perhaps he wanted to liven up the kids a bit. Xu Rongsheng thought for a moment and then asked Li Luo, "Li Luo, do you usually read books?"

Li Luo was a bit stunned by the question, but then he remembered that Xu Rongsheng was a professor of literature, so such a question was quite normal.

However, he wasn't going to pretend to be something he wasn't, stating frankly, "I don't really read those traditional classic novels. I just read some casual books."

"With the internet so developed now, it's true that fewer and fewer young people are reading books," Xu Rongsheng said with a nod. But he didn't urge them to read more as one might expect. Instead, he asked, "Are the books you usually read the kind that are, hmm... webnovels?"

At these words, not only Li Luo, but Lin Xiuhong and Li Guohong beside him also raised their eyebrows.

An unreadable look appeared in Yan Zhusheng's eyes. She glanced at Li Luo, the corners of her eyes curving slightly, then immediately lowered her head to eat, pretending to know nothing.

And Xu Youyu, sitting next to her own father, felt her heart jump. What had gotten into her dad today? Why was he suddenly asking about webnovels?

Could it be that her writing had been exposed?

Was her dad testing and warning her?

With this in mind, Xu Youyu secretly peeked at her father.

On the other side, Li Luo also had a strange look on his face. He then nodded and said, "Yes, webnovels. Does Uncle Xu follow them as well?"

"Hehe, it was just a passing thought. I was chatting with someone at the university today, so I got a little interested," Xu Rongsheng said, making up a casual excuse. He continued, "After all, it's a new form of literature."

"It's just that the teacher I was talking to said that the quality of webnovels nowadays is uneven, and many works are filled with vulgar elements."

"He sort of looked down on webnovels."

"But for a new thing like this, young people's views are definitely different from our generation's, so I'm curious what you all think."

Li Luo looked at Xu Rongsheng. Being asked this, he suddenly recalled several articles and papers Xu Youyu had recommended to him in his past life.

The first author's signature was Xu Rongsheng, who was Xu Youyu's father.

In fact, after Xu Youyu later became successful and famous, Xu Rongsheng had long since put aside his prejudices against webnovels. Influenced by his daughter, he even used his own status in the field of modern and contemporary literature to, in turn, promote a series of studies on web literature.

One passage was written as follows.

"Webnovels have only been around for a little over a decade."

"Thanks to the development of the times and the popularization of the internet, a greater number of people can see these works immediately."

"Of course, they contain a large amount of crudely produced content and various lowbrow tropes, but this is the inevitable growing pains that a new literary form must go through."

"Especially with the popularization of nine-year compulsory education in our country, anyone who has learned Chinese characters can create webnovels."

"Their literary literacy might be close to nil, but because of this, webnovels precisely reflect the achievements of our popularization of compulsory education."

"Otherwise, back in ancient times, among the common people, how many were qualified to write books, and how many were qualified to read them?"

"What's more, the long river of history sifts through everything. The Tang poetry, Song ci, and Yuan qu, when they flourished, were also belittled by the contemporary literati. Didn't many timeless masterpieces from those eras get passed down later?"

"And those crudely made works will naturally disappear into the river of history."

"The same goes for webnovels."

Xu Rongsheng never expected that the young man before him would deliver such a lengthy speech.

The key was that it made a lot of sense.

Hearing this, Xu Rongsheng nodded at once. "You've made some very good points. It's given me some new ways of thinking and new perspectives on webnovels."

He had to attend that provincial online writers' association symposium in February, and he needed to write something to present anyway.

As Xu Rongsheng thought this, he suddenly realized that the content Li Luo just spoke of, with a bit of expansion, would be very suitable for sharing with that group of webnovel authors.

"Here, have a drink." Xu Rongsheng was in a cheerful mood. He raised his glass and clinked it against Li Luo's glass of juice, saying with a smile, "It's rare for a young person to view things from such a rational perspective. I think your way of thinking is very good."

Watching her father clink glasses with Li Luo and listening to the words Li Luo had just said, the guilt Xu Youyu felt for secretly writing webnovels behind her parents' backs seemed to inexplicably lessen a great deal.

Xu Youyu looked at Li Luo's respectful appearance, holding his glass with both hands in a return toast, and a knowing smile appeared on her face.

Suddenly, she felt like she had found material for a scene where the male lead goes to his girlfriend's house for dinner.

What an unexpected surprise.

(End of Chapter)
